audits.title: SipTilSend: Sustainability of a Quality Improvement Initiative to Reduce Pre-operative Fluid Fasting in Orthopaedic Patients – A Re-audit PDSA Cycle
audits.standard: Fasting 6 hours for solids and 2 hours for clear fluids; SipTilSend clear fluids until transfer to theatre
audits.setting: Tertiary university hospital, Cork University Hospital, operative hip fracture patients

cycle1.result: Previous PDSA cycle average fluid fasting 3 h 45 min.

audits.intervention: Reinforcement through staff education, ward prompts and MDT engagement with nursing, orthogeriatric and anaesthetic teams.

cycle2.result: Mean fluid fasting 11.2 hours (median 9.75 hours, range 0-36 hours), worse than previous cycle.

audits.other_findings: No peri-operative aspiration events; compliance with SipTilSend deteriorated over time.
audits.citation: Kapotolo M, Rafar S, Ali M, Abrahams C, Hannon E. SipTilSend: Sustainability of a Quality Improvement Initiative to Reduce Pre-operative Fluid Fasting in Orthopaedic Patients – A Re-audit PDSA Cycle. Age and Ageing. 2026;55(Supplement_2). doi:10.1093/ageing/afag197.039.

audits.title: 291 Pre-Operative Venepuncture: An Audit of The Trauma and Orthopaedic Department at The Royal Sussex County Hospital, Brighton
audits.standard: NICE: routine coagulation or transfusion testing not needed for intermediate or minor surgery unless ASA 3+ or on anticoagulants
audits.setting: Trauma and orthopaedic department, Royal Sussex County Hospital, Brighton

cycle1.result: 92 clotting studies and 200 transfusion samples taken pre-operatively; most for ankle 130/292 (45%) or tibia/fibula 54/292 (18%) procedures; approximately 1168 tests per year costing about £19,616 per year not indicated.

audits.other_findings: Major trauma patients, those on anticoagulants and those with complex histories were excluded; no guidance exists for trauma patients.
audits.citation: Harris H, Antonio T, Hagiga A, Crone D. 291 Pre-Operative Venepuncture: An Audit of The Trauma and Orthopaedic Department at The Royal Sussex County Hospital, Brighton. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_2). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab134.398.

audits.title: A Quality Improvement Project to Assess if Preoperative Trauma Patients Are Receiving Their Prescribed Medications Preoperatively.
audits.standard: Local and national (Royal College of Anaesthetists) guidance that preoperative trauma patients receive prescribed medications while nil by mouth, except anticoagulants, ACE inhibitors and ARBs
audits.setting: Trauma theatre list patients on orthopaedic/surgical wards, Basildon University Hospital

cycle1.result: 16/41 (39%) received their medications correctly; 22 critical drug class omissions; 19 omitted because nil by mouth.

audits.intervention: Poster on drug trolleys listing which medications to give or withhold, meetings with ward managers and nursing staff, and presentation at orthopaedic and anaesthetic audit meetings.

cycle2.result: 25/41 (61%) received their medications correctly; 10 critical drug class omissions; 12 omitted because nil by mouth.

audits.other_findings: Being nil by mouth was the main reason for omission; the abstract states 40 patients in the first round while the text gives 41.
audits.citation: Bhadresha A, Hossain S, Ranjit S, Singh S, Chhetri S. A Quality Improvement Project to Assess if Preoperative Trauma Patients Are Receiving Their Prescribed Medications Preoperatively. Cureus. 2022;14(11):e31928. doi:10.7759/cureus.31928. PMID: 36582572.

audits.title: An Audit on the Pre-operative Fasting Time of Trauma-List Orthopaedic Patients at a District General Hospital in Chichester, United Kingdom.
audits.standard: RCN, AAGBI, European Society of Anaesthesiology and ASA guidelines: fasting of two hours for clear fluids and six hours for solids
audits.setting: Orthopaedic trauma list, St Richard's Hospital, district general hospital, Chichester

cycle1.result: All 50 patients (100%) fasted beyond six hours for solids (mean 15.8 hours, range 9–24) and 49 (98%) beyond two hours for clear fluids (mean 10.5 hours, range 2–20); only 5 (10%) had correct documented fasting instructions; 31 (62%) were 'nil by mouth from midnight'.

audits.other_findings: Staff survey showed poor knowledge: only 42.9% of ward nurses knew the 6 hour/2 hour rule. Only 52% received preoperative IV fluids; a 'sip till send' policy has since been introduced.
audits.citation: Perera H, Wusu A, Mohammad A, Qulaghassi MZ, Abdulkarim A. An Audit on the Pre-operative Fasting Time of Trauma-List Orthopaedic Patients at a District General Hospital in Chichester, United Kingdom. Cureus. 2023;15(11):e48327. doi:10.7759/cureus.48327. PMID: 38024025.

audits.title: Preoperative investigation practices for elective surgical patients: clinical audit.
audits.standard: NICE guideline on routine preoperative tests for elective surgery
audits.setting: Debre Tabor Comprehensive Specialized Hospital; elective general, orthopaedic and gynaecological surgery

cycle1.result: 350 investigations requested; 71 (20.28%) ordered without justification or against NICE recommendations (about 79.71% in line). FBC requested in 240 (97.16%); inappropriate FBC in 45 patients, ECG in 5, urinalysis in 4, hemostasis in 1, CXR in 1. Indicated PT/PTT not done in 4 and HbA1c not done in 4.

audits.other_findings: No patient tested without a clear indication had an abnormal result. Authors recommend an accessible institutional guideline and regular re-audit.
audits.citation: Firde M, Yetneberk T. Preoperative investigation practices for elective surgical patients: clinical audit. BMC Anesthesiol. 2024;24(1):184. doi:10.1186/s12871-024-02557-y. PMID: 38783183.

audits.title: 1385 “Pre-Op Fasting Times Audit in Colorectal Surgery at A University Teaching Hospital”
audits.standard: Trust guidelines on fasting times before major elective surgery
audits.setting: Elective colorectal surgery, Castle Hill Hospital, Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Compliance 10% (2/20) for liquid and 5% (1/20) for solid fasting times.

cycle2.result: Compliance 60% (12/20) for liquid and 0% (0/20) for solid fasting times.

audits.other_findings: Solid fasting times could only improve at the cost of losing theatre time; a further re-audit is planned.
audits.citation: Khan S, Mohideen R, Khan K, Helbren C. 1385 “Pre-Op Fasting Times Audit in Colorectal Surgery at A University Teaching Hospital”. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab259.152.

audits.title: 765 Preoperative Coagulation Screening Audit in General Surgery
audits.standard: British Society of Haematology guidance: no indiscriminate coagulation screening; detailed bleeding history instead

cycle1.result: 19% appropriate requests; 81% of tests done were inappropriate.

cycle2.result: Appropriate requests increased to 56%; inappropriate tests fell to 44%.

audits.other_findings: 148 patients in total across both cycles; each coagulation screen cost an average of £29.42, with an estimated £2971.42 spent on inappropriate requests.
audits.citation: Yomi-Orungbe E, Fazili N. 765 Preoperative Coagulation Screening Audit in General Surgery. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac269.035.

audits.title: SP8.9 Pre-operative blood tests in abscess patients: Audit and cost analysis
audits.standard: NICE NG45: no routine bloods for ASA 1 or 2 patients having minor surgery
audits.setting: Surgical Emergency Unit, Walsall Manor Hospital; incision and drainage of abscess

cycle1.result: 93 patients had pre-operative blood tests; 7 were ASA 3 or higher; cost of unnecessary tests £4,092 (£24,552 per year).

audits.other_findings: Blood tests did not change management; 16 had CRP >50 and 9 had WCC >15.
audits.citation: Tattsbridge J, Hang S, Aukland A, Abdelrahman S. SP8.9 Pre-operative blood tests in abscess patients: Audit and cost analysis. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad241.095.

audits.title: 906 A Prospective Clinical Audit of Pre-Operative Fasting Practices at a Tertiary Care Hospital in India
audits.standard: Indian Society of Anaesthesiologists national preoperative fasting guidelines
audits.setting: Kasturba Medical College Hospital Attavar, tertiary care hospital; ASA 1-2 elective non-obstetric surgery

cycle1.result: Median fasting 10 hours from clear fluids and 12.5 hours from solids; 99% gave an incorrect reason or did not know the reason for fasting.

audits.intervention: Patient information leaflets in English and the local language distributed to every ward for patients the day before surgery; surgical and anaesthetic trainees and nurses made aware of the findings.

cycle2.result: Median fasting 3 hours from clear fluids and 11 hours from solids; 35% knew the correct reason, 50% gave an incorrect reason, 15% did not know.

audits.other_findings: Solid fasting remained prolonged despite the fall in clear fluid fasting.
audits.citation: Mendonca J, Upadya M, Arora M. 906 A Prospective Clinical Audit of Pre-Operative Fasting Practices at a Tertiary Care Hospital in India. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad258.157.

audits.title: SP3.02 Unnecessary Preoperative Blood Tests for Patients Undergoing Abscess Incision and Drainage: A Closed-Loop Audit
audits.standard: NICE: ASA 1 or 2 patients should not receive preoperative blood tests for abscess incision and drainage
audits.setting: General surgery department, Victoria Hospital Kirkaldy

cycle1.result: 71 abscess I&D cases, 55 ASA 1 or 2; 50/55 (91%) ASA 1–2 cases had routine bloods, costing £2,151.

audits.intervention: Findings disseminated to the department and posters advising not to take bloods for routine abscess I&D.

cycle2.result: 63 cases, 55 ASA 1 or 2; 15/55 (27%) had routine bloods, costing £406.

audits.other_findings: Saving of £1745 over 4 months, projected at more than £5,000 per year.
audits.citation: Abhari R, Sakib N, Proctor M. SP3.02 Unnecessary Preoperative Blood Tests for Patients Undergoing Abscess Incision and Drainage: A Closed-Loop Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_13). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf166.036.

audits.title: TPW 9.02 Routine Preoperative Investigations in Low-Risk Elective Inguinal Hernia Patients: A Closed-Loop Audit
audits.standard: NICE guidance on routine preoperative tests by ASA grade
audits.setting: Elective inguinal hernia repair, large tertiary centre, The Newcastle upon Tyne Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Poor overall compliance with NICE guidelines (figures not given).

audits.intervention: Results presented locally; updated trust guidance and a digital decision-aid tool.

cycle2.result: ASA 1 unnecessary tests fell by 20.5% (FBC), 21.4% (haemostasis), 22.6% (U&E), 33.0% (ECG); ASA 2 fell by 75.0%, 16.7%, 11.9% and 9.4%.

audits.other_findings: No lung function tests or ABG in either cycle; cycle 2 was limited to one of the trust's two hospitals.
audits.citation: Wong T, Khatri K, Pugh E. TPW 9.02 Routine Preoperative Investigations in Low-Risk Elective Inguinal Hernia Patients: A Closed-Loop Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag087.403.
